Natural Specimens
Polished Fluorite Heart and Raw Stone Collection
Mineral, Stone, and Seashell Set
Approx. 1" to 1.75" Dimensions
Unsigned
This eclectic collection features four distinct natural elements, headlined by a hand-polished green and blue fluorite heart. The fluorite exhibits characteristic translucency and internal crystalline structures typical of the mineral. Accompanying the heart is a weathered river stone with a smooth, water-worn texture, a raw mineral specimen with granular surface detail, and a naturally aged bivalve seashell with distinct ribbing and radial symmetry.
Polished fluorite heart displays vibrant shades of teal and forest green
Rough mineral specimen features crystalline inclusions and earthy tones
Natural bivalve seashell shows classic radial symmetry and weathered white finish
Condition:
Excellent natural condition. The fluorite heart is polished to a high gloss with minor internal fissures typical of the mineral. The raw stones and shell show natural textures, weathering, and geological characteristics consistent with their natural and geological origins.

279237796.description:
Vintage Chalet Market Montana Sausage Box with Rocks Minerals Fossils Lot
This listing includes a vintage Chalet Market of Montana sausage box repurposed as a storage container for a collection of rocks, minerals, and possible fossil specimens. The assortment features various petrified wood, agate, jasper, obsidian, quartz, and other stones. Some pieces are shaped or fractured, suggesting ancient tools or natural artifacts. Specimens range from small chips to larger fragments and are presented both loose and within a small plastic display case. The box shows significant wear and tape residue, while the stones are unpolished with natural variations and textures. Suitable for collectors, geology enthusiasts, or educational use.

278650394.description: This lot includes 12 vintage glass telephone pole insulators primarily manufactured by Hemingray and Whitall Tatum. The insulators are made of clear, aqua, and light green glass and feature embossed branding and model numbers, including Hemingray-42 and Whitall Tatum No. 1. The condition varies among pieces, with some showing visible chips, cracks, and signs of wear consistent with age and use. These insulators are historically significant for telegraph and power line applications and are commonly collected or used as decorative items. Overall, the set is used with minor to moderate damage on certain pieces. Approximately 3.75" D, 4" H each.
